transcript: I went to go see rent at Paper Mill Playhouse, which literally just closed on Sunday. So sorry you. You can't go see it. I still want to talk about it, however. I think it's really interesting to see what people are starting to do with these non replica productions of rent, because I feel like there's a lot to. And this production did something really, really cool, which was essentially make it a memory play. They set up this interesting framing device at the beginning where Mark is looking through tapes and he pulls it out. And what he pulls out is the footage that he shot during the time that rent takes place. Which I think is a really, really, really cool concept. I just don't think it went far enough with it because Mark was just played by one actor, Zachary no Pizer, who did an absolutely fantastic job. But it was hard to tell which Mark we were seeing on stage. Was this the Mark that's looking back on his memories, or is this the Mark that is actively going through the events of the past? But I would love to see this concept be tried again with just 2 different marks. Cast it like a beautiful noise where you have a much older Mark that is looking back and then the Mark of the 19 90s. The cast in this production was absolutely stellar. I thought they made some really interesting casting decisions, and ultimately, I thought all of the characters had great chemistry with each other. I could believe that this was a group of friends that I was watching on stage, but they were only good when I could hear them. And I've never seen a show with this many missed my cues. Paper Mill, I'm tagging you in this video because I cannot stress enough how much this needs to be fixed before the next show. I saw the 3rd to last performance of rent, and we were missing entire verses in songs because the mics weren't being turned on. But in moments when the mic should not have been on at all, like when 2 characters are embracing, the mics were on and so we just got a bunch of static. I have seen high school productions with sound better than this. And this wasn't just a one off for my performance because I talked to other people that saw this and this seemed to be consistently an issue with this production. So I cannot stress enough, please, please, please get this fixed before the next production. Especially because the next production is Gatsby, and like, like we need good sound for that show. Please. Overall, I'm really glad I went to go see this production. There were a lot of performers that were new to me that I cannot wait to see what they do next. And I really just love rent as a show. And while I didn't really Agree with a lot of the directorial decisions made in this production. I love that it tried something new, and I hope, especially as rent is being produced in practically every regional theater across the country, including my own in Colorado Springs, I hope that we get to see more productions like this one, where they try to find something new in the material, both in the way that it is directed and in the way that it is cast.
